full_judgment:
7. Mr. ASM Sayem Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (in short, the Ain) is a special law and that Ain, 2003 does not contain any provision for appointing a receiver over the mortgaged property. In this regard he further submits that while allowing the prayer of the respondent bank by the Adalat there was no ingredient available to attract the provision of Order XL, rule 1 read with section 69A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (in short, the Act, 1882). He also goes to argue that section 69A of the said Act is a contingent provision being enshrined for the purpose of section 69(1) and (2) of the said Act. Accordingly, he submits that since the respondent bank has instituted the mortgage suit and prayed for mortgage decree hence, section 69 as a whole and for that matter section 69A has no manner of application while invoking Order XL, rule I of the Code. As such, order No. 42 dated 22-1-2023 passed by the respondent No.1 is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and hence, of no legal effect. 

 13. The petitioner No. 1, the principal loanee and petitioner No. 2, a 3rd party guarantor, however, have assailed the impugned order of appointment of receiver by the Adalat dated 22-1-2023 on the ground that on the face of execution of collateral security as security to the loan amount appointing a receiver over the mortgaged property under Order XL, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable in the eye of law. Moreover, because of the said order the petitioners are now deprived of their right to enjoying the possession of the properties in question prior to passing the decree in the said suit; thus, defeating the cause of justice. 

 23. Order XL, rule 1 of the Code confers wide discretion upon the Court for appointment of a receiver even before decree, but such discretion is exercised if it appears to be just and convenient after consideration of the whole of the circumstances of the case which necessitates said appointment. Order XL, rule 1 of the Code is accordingly quoted below for ready reference:— 

 (a) appoint a receiver of any property, whether before or after decree;
